text:
Marta (Marketing): Heads-up: product wants a compact battlecard and landing routing for the benchmark launch. Need: 1-page AE snapshot, two-line SDR hooks, and a HubSpot routing map that surfaces high-cost risk to AEs.
Ike (Product): Core proof points: 1) p95 stability under contention, 2) identical API across hosted/dedicated/private, 3) clear knobs to control unit cost (batching, cache, quant). I'll export microbench CSVs.
Vera (Sales): SDR hooks (quick):
- Startup: "How do you avoid surprise inference bills when usage grows?"
- Enterprise: "We make serving predictable across environments so ops can sleep at night."
I'll make 2 variants per persona.
Cam (Growth): Routing pseudo-rule for HubSpot (prototype):
```
if (form.role == 'engineer' && est_monthly_tokens > 5e8) route = 'ae-tech-demo';
else if (company.size >= 500 || est_monthly_tokens > 1e9) route = 'enterprise-sales';
else route = 'marketing-nurture';
```
Add hidden est_monthly_tokens field and a checkbox for "interested in private deployment".
ops-bot: Canary deploy for demo infra set for Wed 11:00 PT. CI: https://ci.redwood/deploy/987 (green).
Marta (Marketing): Webinar flow idea: 6m market problem, 12m benchmark story (real customer example + chart), 20m live demo showing fallback chain and rollback, 10m Q&A. Need a micro-slides pack + AE 1-liner.
Ike (Product): Bench plan: compare ModelY on CloudProvider_A managed endpoint, self-hosted baseline, Redwood-hosted, and Redwood-dedicated. Metrics: cold p95, sustained p95 at 600 concurrent sessions, tokens_per_usd. Will include hardware, batch settings, quant settings, and caveats.
Vera (Sales): AE one-liner candidates: "Redwood: serving primitives so your product's latency and cost don't surprise you." or "Ship features, not ops runbooks." Which resonates?
Cam (Growth): CTA experiments: "Join the benchmark webinar" vs "See your cost estimate". If est_monthly_tokens > 1e9 show calendar CTA to AE in confirmation email. We'll run by referral source.
Marta (Marketing): Competitive claims to finalize: vs Cloud APIs -> "Simpler model access vs predictable serving in production". vs Self-host -> "We take the kernel/config heavy lifting out of your ops backlog." Keep lines <20 words.
Ike (Product): I'll add a short note on quant tradeoffs: "Lite quantization reduces cost but may change tail-case quality; include eval set in the microbench."
Vera (Sales): Procurement bullets for battlecard: pricing (usage + reserved), SLA options for Dedicated, data residency/private deployment note. Keep them 2 lines each.
Cam (Growth): I'll draft the HubSpot mapping and add tests: 1) form-based routing; 2) hidden token estimate capture; 3) escalation email with AE calendar. Share mapping in doc.
Marta (Marketing): Owners: Ike -> battlecard + CSVs; Vera -> SDR lines + procurement bullets; Cam -> HubSpot routing + CTA tests; Marta -> slide pack + copy. Deadline: drafts by Thu noon.
Ike (Product): Will also include a tiny microbench table header suggestion: [env, seq_len, batch_size, p95_ms, tokens_per_usd].
Vera (Sales): I'll compress SDR rebuttals vs managed cloud and self-host into one-liners for quick use.
Marta (Marketing): Thanks. I'll stitch the deck and post a draft link here: https://docs.redwood/launch/battlecard-draft — please comment directly. :rocket:
